reviews.title: A perfect case study of how much of a cancer greed is upon the mobile app landscape
reviews.text:
Swipe left to delete a random photo from your camera roll, swipe right to keep it? Pretty fun idea, pretty simple to implement, and it was pretty easy for me to download the app when I first saw it. It has you stare at 30 seconds of glowing reviews and all the great numbers the app has. Then it runs you through a few questions to “customize the experience” to you. All is well, looks like I’m almost able to use the app! Nope. Here’s a three day free trial for you to enjoy before you have to pay… $10 a week to use their app. $520 a year. But not to fret, you can get almost 85% off if you pay for their yearly subscription of $80! 

I don’t think I’ve ever left a review on an app in my entire life until now. How this (likely AI vibecoded in under 10 min) app got so many positive reviews bewilders me. The only thing that makes sense is that they didn’t force you to pay an actually clinically insane amount when the app came out, they gathered their good reviews, and then turned around and started trying to nickel and dime everyone. Don’t waste your time, don’t get this app. If the devs are reading this, shame on you, I hope there’s a tiny sharp piece of wood in your socks that pokes into your ankles and then when you try to find it, it’s like it was never there.

reviews.title: Long time user of swipe wipe… very disappointed
reviews.text:
I’ve used Swipe Wipe for YEARS, and I’m genuinely disappointed to the point that I’ve had to uninstall it. What used to be a simple, convenient app has become practically unusable because of the overwhelming number of ads.

You can barely scroll through your own photos or delete anything without being interrupted by another advertisement. And to make matters worse, HALF of these ads crash the app. When you reopen it, you’re immediately hit with ANOTHER ad, only to end up right back where you started. It’s an endless cycle of ads, crashes, reopening, and more ads. At this point, using the actual app feels like an afterthought.

I understand that developers need to generate revenue, but there is a difference between reasonable advertising and making an app so frustrating that its basic functionality is practically inaccessible.

And no, I’m not paying a subscription just for the convenience of swiping through and deleting my own photos. That’s an unreasonable ask for what should be a straightforward utility app.

It’s incredibly disappointing to see an app I’ve used and enjoyed for years deteriorate this badly. You’ve managed to turn a useful, simple tool into an advertisement simulator. Uninstalled.

reviews.title: Deleted THOUSANDS of photos without my permission, TWICE

I gave the app another chance because I thought maybe it was a mistake that I made and not the app, and that it wouldn't happen again. It worked fine until today when I tried to find any pictures of myself from 2023, and couldn't find ANY in August and September even though I knew I took a lot of selfies at that time. SO many pictures and videos of me and my friends from years ago are gone. So much documentation from my first year of college is gone permanently and I KNOW I never would have deleted it myself on the app. Some of these pictures I remember seeing in my camera roll just a few days ago, and are now gone despite the fact I didn't use SwipeWipe in those past days. The total count of photos I had also seems a lot lower than what it was before, like thousands lower. I deleted the app so it wouldn't do anything else, but redownloaded it because I thought maybe some of my old photos. But I can't even get into the app without agreeing to the free trial. I'm really, really upset and don't know what to do.

reviews.title: Eh
reviews.text: Seems like a good idea in hindsight, but it’s the money thirsting where they really get you. I like the idea of the app and being able to choose what photos to keep and delete instead of going through your camera roll is an awesome idea, but I wish it wasn’t such a money grab. For 10 dollars a week I would rather go through my camera roll and just delete photos. Maybe if it was cheaper or ten dollars for a month or something better like that I would pay, because the app is really cool and a good idea, but paying that much is just not defendable just to delete photos, when there’s a much bigger second option. Besides that, I wouldn’t pay 10 dollars a week for a glitchy app. I go to a month and it gives me 13 billion ads and no photos then says I’m done and keeps all of them? And if I want to actually go through them how the app says it works (aka the whole point of the app) I have to tap each one and say keep or delete individually. What??? And for people like me that don’t take a lot of photos, one month is like 10 photos and I would rather go through my camera roll than go through the 10 photos and have to wait 8 hours to go through more. Anyways, I just don’t think the subscription is justifiable for the app when you can go through your camera roll for free. Maybe it saves you 1 minute but it’s not worth it unless you take a gazillion photos and are very patient. Cool idea though

reviews.title: Loved it until it lost all of my progress
reviews.text: This app is expensive which I was okay with because I’ve been avoiding a deep clean of my camera roll for years. I think I started with 75k and am down closer to 30k since the new year.(2 months) recently it’s been saying months aren’t completed then when I open the months it says confirm these are the photos you want to keep. Makes sense because I already went through them. Then back to the Home Screen the app doesn’t cross the month out. Even though I go in and confirm the ones I want to keep over and over. I hope this makes sense. It didn’t delete anything it shouldn’t. It’s just visually not keeping accurate track of what I’ve already gone through which is so frustrating and unsatisfying. If I want and unsatisfying experience I’ll delete my photos from my camera roll for free.

reviews.title: For the 1% only
reviews.text:
Look, I get it. You can’t just run an app for free with no ads or limitations without a premium option. But who in their right mind decided that this app is worth $40 A MONTH?? I pay less than this for internet, utilities, and car insurance. You guys are completely out of touch with reality if you think this app is worth a top spot on the average person’s budgeting sheet. This app seems to be marketed towards younger people who definitely don’t have that kind of money, making it seem like the only customers they really want money from is those with ludicrous generational wealth or something.
I think a $25 lifetime/yearly or $3 monthly premium option would attract a lot more people into spending money on your app, because let’s be so for real, $40 a month in 2026 isn’t happening for 99% of people. Devs are genuinely delusional about the worth of the service they provide, or they think only people with insane disposable income deserve to delete some pictures limit-free.

reviews.title: Terrible app
reviews.text: I got this app because all the reviews said it was really good and it was FREE!! Little did I know u have to pay. So I go onto the app and it asks u a few questions or u can skip then its talking about a free trial so I go back onto the other reviews and 1 of the reviews I see say that u do have to pay so I just delete the app immediately. I think this app should definitely be free because all i want to do is clear out my photos efficiently.

reviews.title: Great concept - app is basically unusable
reviews.text:
Have had this app show up in my ads heaps lately so thought I would give it a go. Signed up to the free trial to see the app at its full potential. Approximately every 45 seconds the app crashes completely so it’s extremely hard to actually use the app for its purpose. I’ve managed to delete 20 photos in 30 minutes - I feel I could’ve done triple this if the app didn’t crash or just without the app full
stop.
